newsitem.title: UK: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.
newsitem.headline: EU seen awarding up to 60,000 T sugar at tender.

text.p: The European Union (EU) is expected to award as much as 60,000 tonnes of current series white sugar at its weekly tender later on Wednesday, traders said.
But while 60,000 tonnes was the upper end of the consensus of estimates, 30,000 tonnes was a more likely figure, they said.
Last week the EU awarded 34,750 tonnes in its tender.
This week's maximum restitution level was estimated at 43.862 Ecus (European currency units) per 100 kilos of sugar after the 43.835 Ecus awarded last week.
Licences are currently valid until the end of August. Cumulatively, the tonnage awards for 1996/97 are still lagging behind the equivalent stage in 1995/96
"It's catching up...cumulatively, it's not all that much different from last year but still behind what the Commission would like," said one trader.
As of March 5, this year's total stood at 1,597,900 tonnes, compared with 1,603,398 tonnes on March 6, 1996.
"They're getting closer to last year but last year was generally regarded as a disaster -- they were 300,000 tonnes short of what they thought they were going to be able to export," said another.
"If that happened again this year, you begin to wonder where all the sugar is going to go," he said. --Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
